(a) the DDR and autophagic pathways are linked by acetylation, and (b) the link between DDR and acetylation is conserved in mammals.

the acetylated state of CtIP and Exol is important to control their activity, that this acetylation is regulated by HDACs, that HDACs are involved in the DDR, and that this DDR-HDAC connection may be relevant in cancer.
the acetylations of DDR proteins are controlled by HDACs, and that this control is linked to autophagy, which in turn is a target of anticancer agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of histone acetylation in the regulation of DNA damage responses and its potential implications in the development of cancer.

the identification of the molecular pathways involved in the control and deregulation of the DNA damage and repair response in mammalian cells, and with the development of pharmacological strategies for the treatment of cancer.
the role of acetylation and HDACs in the control of DNA damage repair and autophagy, with particular focus on the potential therapeutic implications of these findings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acetylated CtIP is a new player that is required for the activation of the DDR and that it is involved in autophagy.
the acetylated proteins involved in DNA repair, and the autophagy process itself, are not yet fully understood.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are now beginning to understand the role of acetylation in DNA damage and repair.
HDAC inhibitors are a class of drugs that have the ability to modulate the DDR through the control of acetylation and autophagy, and that this modulation can be harnessed in cancer therapy.

the HDAC inhibitors are not only inhibitors for histone deacetylation, but also for non-histone deacetylations, including those of DNA damage response ( DDR ) proteins, which are critical for cell survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that

HDAC inhibitors are likely to be effective anticancer agents not only because of their ability to induce histone acetylation, but because of their capacity to modulate acetylations on non-histone substrates.
HDACs are involved in the regulation of the DDR and autophagic processes.

acetylation of CtIP by HDAC6 and HDAC8 leads to the recruitment and activation of autophagy, which degrades the acetyl-lysine–binding proteins Exo1 and CtIP, thus preventing their action in DNA damage repair.
